lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. Amy gets a dimmer.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, busy, cheerful, husband who knows the rules] Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. Amy gets a dimmer.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. Also, why are you sticky?
lines.script: [thick New York accent, beaming dad, warm, then puzzled and a little grossed out] Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. Also, why are you sticky?

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. Before lunch.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, casual brag, counting on fingers, smug on the last two words] Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. Before lunch.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. I got a truck and two girls. Living the song.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, easy, amused, singing the last three words a little] Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. I got a truck and two girls. Living the song.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. It was a playoff game. We lost.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, dry, deadpan, a little proud of the story, grim on the last two words] Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. It was a playoff game. We lost.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. And I built that deck.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, soft, sincere, then a proud joke about the deck] Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. And I built that deck.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, cheerful, relieved, a little sheepish about the bread] Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, generous, then a conspiratorial whisper] Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, tired teacher, counting the years, dry on Gary] Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: It's store-bought.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, flat confession, a little guilty] It's store-bought.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, satisfied, then hands full and impatient, sharp on the copper] The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: It lights up. Every letter. I'm an electrician, Gracie. It was never going to just hang there.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, proud, a little offended at the question, fond on Gracie] It lights up. Every letter. I'm an electrician, Gracie. It was never going to just hang there.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Hold this. No, the other end. It's the OTHER banner. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, hands full, impatient, then sharp warning about the copper] Hold this. No, the other end. It's the OTHER banner. Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Conference night is over. I survived. I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, exhausted teacher, slumping, deadpan relief] Conference night is over. I survived. I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. She brings one every conference night.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, perking up, reverent, like describing a holiday] Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. She brings one every conference night.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Don't tell Gary. Gary eats the whole thing.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, conspiratorial whisper, then flat disapproval of Gary] Don't tell Gary. Gary eats the whole thing.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. That's allowed. It's in the contract.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, low, hiding, conspiratorial, a tired teacher who has read the contract] Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. That's allowed. It's in the contract.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. Every lunch in there has a name on it. Read the labels.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, warning, deadpan, like a safety briefing] If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. Every lunch in there has a name on it. Read the labels.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, friendly greeting mid-task, hands full, quick warning] Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? Both. Correct. Go get 'em.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, goofy proud dad, calling them over, quick quiz voice, then sending them off with a clap] Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? Both. Correct. Go get 'em.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Long Island born. Country music raised. Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, shrugging, amused at himself, matter of fact] Long Island born. Country music raised. Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Big game tonight. If you hear yelling, that's me. If you hear crying, that's also me.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, grinning, hyped, then mock-serious on the crying part] Big game tonight. If you hear yelling, that's me. If you hear crying, that's also me.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. I know. It's on the list.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, calm heads-up, then sheepish, it has been on the list a while] Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. I know. It's on the list.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, easygoing, eager, goofy proud dad, deadpan on the strong opinion] Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, warm, cheerful, a little distracted, firm on the ladder] Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, easygoing, dry, a little rueful, it has been June for a while] No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.

lines.speaker: Justin
lines.text: Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, relaxed, amused, no hard feelings] Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
